name: Jehoram
overview: Jehoram was a male king of Israel and the son of Ahab. His reign is noted in the books of 2 Kings, where he is identified as King Jehoram or Joram. Beyond his royal status and lineage, no specific tribal affiliation or additional personal notes are recorded.
namesAndTitles: Jehoram's name means 'y-h-v-h exalts,' reflecting a theophoric element honoring the Lord, though the name itself was not given by God. He is also referred to by the titles 'King of Israel' and 'King Jehoram,' emphasizing his royal authority. The variant 'Joram' similarly means 'y-h-v-h is exalted,' underscoring the same divine exaltation theme.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Jehoram was the son of Ahab, establishing his royal lineage within Israel's monarchy. No other family relationships are detailed beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Jehoram's significance lies in his role as a king of Israel during a turbulent period. As the son of Ahab, his reign reflects the continuation of Ahab's legacy. Although further details of his actions are limited here, his position as king situates him within the broader biblical narrative of Israel's monarchy and its spiritual challenges.
